system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — not agreed or cleared.** The Seller’s “FINAL”, principal-agreement and market-standard assertions are not buyer authority. No Amelia Frost approval has been given for the cap or time-limit fallbacks. DD references below are Seller-supplied descriptions, not independently verified or refreshed source evidence.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4,800,000. | 25% / AUD 6,000,000; 20% only with prior written Amelia Frost authority identifying the draft. | **Counter at 25%.** Matching an available fallback does not authorise its use. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds and the deductible mechanism.** The proposal materially excludes otherwise recoverable losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months for general warranties; 18 months only with Amelia Frost’s written approval; no category spillover. | **Restore 24 months and confine its scope.** Neither the shorter period nor its broader application is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share general caps and deadlines. | Separate 100% cap and at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bars. | **Reject general-regime treatment.** Ownership and capacity risks require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding carve-out throughout.** This protection is mandatory and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Specific fair disclosure sufficient to explain the nature and scope of each matter; no whole-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject blanket disclosure and require warranty-linked particulars.** Document availability alone must not extinguish warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for Buyer/adviser knowledge or anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any negotiated knowledge qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as proposed.** It improperly transfers undisclosed and discoverable risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; delivery of written consent satisfies the condition, despite no final consent or conditions evidence supplied. | Effective consent **and evidence all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Make both requirements Completion conditions and obtain current evidence.** Delivery alone does not resolve a material customer dependency representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; security release after Completion; no repayment or final discharge evidenced. | Current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; any deferred release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and Amelia Frost approval**. | **Require a documented Completion discharge mechanism.** The current proposal leaves the acquired business exposed to outstanding security. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses are a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Explicit treatment of DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrably Seller-funded. | **Verify triggers and on-costs, then revise funds flow or document Seller funding.** Silent omission risks the Buyer bearing an unprovided Completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity restricted to SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open without independent payment verification or confirmatory assignment. | Broader protection for associated IP ownership/transfer defects and resulting claims and losses, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-transfer cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment and effective transfer.** Neither payment nor non-payment of AUD 180,000 is independently established, and payment exposure alone does not cover title risk. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification remain unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, assess notification obligations and require continuing updates. | **Require preservation, investigation and reporting commitments; reserve conclusions.** There is no established breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, accrual, avoidability, termination rights and ordinary-course status. | **Investigate before deciding contractual or price treatment.** Neither automatic Debt classification or deduction nor the Seller’s ordinary-course assertion is justified on this record. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations extend across Claims; title, tax and IP are swept into the general regime. | Distinct Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant treatment, with express scope and precedence preventing hidden general-regime overrides. | **Remove cross-category catch-alls and check all cross-references.** Otherwise general limitations could silently defeat separately negotiated obligations and remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 internal share register is treated as evidence of 100% title. | Independent corroborating evidence of ownership, title, encumbrances and authority, alongside the register. | **Keep title verification outstanding and obtain independent evidence.** A supplied internal register is a source to test, not independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranty positions described as settled under the general regime. | Keep both open for express negotiation of scope, exclusions, caps, periods and relevant indemnities; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Reject “settled” status and retain express reservations.** Seller assertions cannot resolve outstanding buyer positions or establish authority. |

**Next step:** Obtain the underlying DD documents and current updates—particularly for disclosures stated only as at 22 September 2026—and test them against the complete SPA before clearing any issue.
=== END ADVICE ===
